items.desc: The former Australian opener, who won every Cricket World Cups, was announced as the third foreign signing for the third season of the NPL by Kathmandu Gorkhas on Tuesday.

items.title: Three appointed high court judges
items.desc: The Judicial Council has appointed Supreme Court Registrar Bhadrakali Pokharel, District Judge Himlal Belbase and Gajendra Bahadur Singh as high court judges, while also approving judicial transfers and new appointments.

items.title: How China is preparing for the risk of AI escaping human control
items.desc: China is tightening rules, safety standards and state oversight as it prepares for increasingly autonomous AI systems to evade safeguards, replicate or act beyond human control.

items.title: Ten families at risk as landslide threatens Baitadi village
items.desc: A landslide that destroyed one house has left the entire village vulnerable, prompting authorities to urge households to relocate to safer areas.

items.title: Footbridges rise again from flood wreckage
items.desc: Repairs and reconstruction are underway on 53 footbridges damaged by the August 26 flood along the Trishuli corridor, restoring vital links to markets, schools, health services and jobs.

items.title: Weeks after the Nepal flood disaster, families of the missing hold out hope
items.desc: With 5,130 people still missing in Nepal and hundreds unaccounted for in China, families are scouring hospitals, contacting authorities and tracking digital clues for any sign their loved ones survived.

items.title: Government rolls out sweeping capital market reform plan
items.desc: The 21-point package seeks to ease IPO rules, restructure Nepse, expand bond and margin trading and cut capital gains tax.

items.title: ‘Last Man In Tower’: Ben Rekhi’s film dilutes its source material’s amused cynicism
items.desc: Rekhi’s film on Aravind Adiga’s novel is passable in theory but leaves more to be desired towards the end.

items.title: Foreign stars raise the bar for Nepal’s volleyball league
items.desc: While overseas athletes swept individual honours throughout the tournament, players and coaches view the skill gap not as a setback, but as a long-overdue bridge to professionalising the national game.

items.title: 472 undocumented workers, including Nepalis, detained in Kuala Lumpur raids
items.desc: Raid is part of an extended migrant repatriation programme.

items.title: After the floods, Nepal’s survivors face the uncertainty of starting over
items.desc: With homes destroyed, families shattered and winter approaching, thousands of displaced people remain caught between unsafe villages and temporary shelters.

items.title: The ’80s are trending. But AI nostalgia comes with a hidden environmental cost
items.desc: Every AI-generated image requires computing power, electricity and cooling, raising questions about the environmental price of a seemingly harmless online fad.

items.title: Private sector bears bulk of Bhotekoshi flood losses
items.desc: A preliminary government assessment estimates damage and economic losses at Rs408 billion. Nearly 4,800 businesses and 7,570 homes were damaged, while 13 hydropower projects and five solar plants were hit.

items.title: Why the government must be stopped from chaining the central bank governor
items.desc: Proposed changes to the NRB Bill threaten monetary stability and regulatory independence.

items.title: How Nepal can take the global lead on Himalayan climate strategy
items.desc: By championing predictive monitoring, resilient engineering and managed retreat instead of mere compensation, the country can reshape international climate policy for vulnerable mountainous nations.

items.title: Why fixing Nepal’s government takes more than just copying the rulebook
items.desc: As public issues grow increasingly interconnected and citizens demand faster, more transparent services, Nepal’s conventional administrative reforms are falling short.

items.title: Flood survivors face water shortages, disease risk in crowded holding centres
items.desc: More than 3,600 people are staying in 37 holding centres across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading districts. No major outbreak has been reported, but cases of colds, coughs and viral fever are common.

items.title: Nepal begins overhaul of school curriculum, with AI and indigenous knowledge in focus
items.desc: Nationwide consultations seek to reshape Nepal’s school curriculum by integrating AI, disaster preparedness, entrepreneurship and indigenous knowledge.

items.title: India approves additional 654 MW power exports to Nepal
items.desc: The additional supply is expected to help Nepal manage winter power shortages after floods damaged hydropower plants and transmission infrastructure.

items.title: Finance Minister Wagle to visit India on September 17-18
items.desc: The two-day visit will be the first high-level visit from Nepal to India since the August 26 floods devastated parts of the country.

items.title: Deuba faction cracks as 31 leaders line up behind Thapa
items.desc: The leaders’ move deals a blow to Sher Bahadur Deuba’s push for a parallel convention, as the Gagan Thapa-led Congress opens doors to members of the former central committee.

items.title: Himalayas approaching tipping point, millions of livelihoods at stake: Report
items.desc: Faster glacier melt is threatening water security and increasing the risk of glacial lake floods across the Hindu Kush-Himalaya, putting millions of people downstream at risk.

items.title: US approves $1m forensic support for Nepal flood victim identification
items.desc: The new funding takes US humanitarian, health and forensic assistance following the floods to more than $5 million.

items.title: Beijing to ban drone possession, storage from November 15
items.desc: The new rules are part of a broader push to tighten airspace security, with limited exemptions for emergency, research, industrial and other authorised operations.

items.title: Nepal Airlines jet grounded in Japan, disrupting international flights
items.desc: The airline’s only operational widebody remains in Narita after an engine problem affected a flight carrying 226 passengers, with Doha services also at risk.

items.title: Flood blocks Jajarkot-Dolpa road, sweeps away homes and shops
items.desc: Torrential rain triggered flooding in Jajarkot’s Nalgad area, disrupting transport on the Bheri Corridor and destroying homes, businesses and other structures.

items.title: Nepal tunnel survivor finds solace in village homecoming
items.desc: Rescued after nine days trapped in a hydropower tunnel, Sanjay Sah returned to his family in a village still mourning workers missing after last month’s disaster.

items.title: Sweden’s centre-left bloc leads close election against right-wing government
items.desc: A narrow early lead for Magdalena Andersson’s centre-left bloc could end Ulf Kristersson’s four-year government and put Sweden’s hardening migration policies under review.
